subject: Proposal: Reserved GPU Commitment + EU/APAC failover addendum
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Murphy <alex.murphy@acme.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 16:12:00 -0400
Subject: Proposal: Reserved GPU Commitment + EU/APAC failover addendum

Alex — attaching a concise amendment to the current Dedicated contract that covers the renewal term and the multi-region expansion we discussed on the call. High-level summary below: 

- Term: 12 months (renewal start 2026-07-01)
- Commitment: +48 reserved A100-equivalent GPUs (24 EU, 24 APAC) for base throughput
- Burst pool: additional ephemeral burst capacity up to 12 GPUs per region during peak windows (billing at 1.2x base rate)
- Throughput guarantee: baseline 10K generated tokens/min sustained per region, 95th pct latency target for 128-token responses: EU < 85ms, APAC < 120ms
- Failover: cross-region fallback with cold-warm standby pools. RPO: stateless; RTO target 90s for new session fallback, traffic-level failover routing in 3 tiers (local -> regional -> global)
- Pricing: blended reserved rate with regional uplift for APAC at +8%; see attached capacity_matrix_acme.xlsx for scenarios and unit economics

Attachments: RWI_Acme_Reserved_Commitment_Amendment_v1.pdf (redline-ready), capacity_matrix_acme.xlsx, latency_sla_table.csv.

Immediate asks: please confirm the EU/APAC sizing split and whether procurement prefers a single amendment or separate region-specific SOWs. Happy to jump on a short call to walk through the failure modes and traffic shaping approach.

Thanks,
Monica
Monica Patel
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Murphy <alex.murphy@acme.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acme.ai
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 09:28:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Proposal: Reserved GPU Commitment + EU/APAC failover addendum

Monica — thanks for the summary and files. A couple of clarifying questions from procurement and infra before we escalate to legal: 

1) Cold-warm standby: can you clarify whether the standby pools will incur idle compute billing (i.e., will we be paying reserved commitment for those GPUs when they are in warm state)?
2) SLA & credits: the draft mentions latency targets. What financial SLA/credits are tied to the regional latency (EU / APAC) and to cross-region failover availability?
3) Burst billing: procurement asks for an example month with traffic pattern that triggers burst — can you show math for cost at 40% burst utilization for 2 weeks?

Also: ACME would prefer separate region SOWs if it lets us manage our own compliance boundaries per region (GDPR/DS-PSP).

Would appreciate if you can send a short note that we can share with procurement summarizing billing behavior for standby pools and the credit ladder.

Best,
Alex Murphy
VP, ML Platforms — Acme AI

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Murphy <alex.murphy@acme.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, procurement@acme.ai
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: Reserved GPU Commitment + EU/APAC failover addendum

Alex / procurement team — answers inline, and I attached a short one-page billing explainer you can pass to procurement.

1) Standby billing: reserved GPUs in "warm" standby for regional failover are billed at the committed reserved rate (they count toward the reserved commitment). Ephemeral burst instances are billed separately at the burst rate when active; we do not double-bill reserved + burst for the same active instance. If you prefer, we can structure the contract to only count base reserved for billing and treat warm-standby as included for up to X hours/month (we can negotiate X).

2) SLA & credits: proposed credit ladder in the amendment (see RWI_Acme_Reserved_Commitment_Amendment_v1.pdf):
   - Regional availability (per-region) < 99.5% monthly -> 10% credit on monthly committed fees
   - Regional availability < 98% -> 25% credit
   - Latency SLO (95th pct for 128-token) misses by >40% -> 5% credit; misses by >75% -> 15% credit.
   - Cross-region failover unavailability during customer traffic (failed to route to alternate region within 180s) -> 20% credit
Note: Credits capped at 50% monthly committed fees and subject to post-incident validation & customer-provided traffic logs.

3) Burst billing example: attached capacity_matrix_acme.xlsx tab 'BurstExample' — quick summary: base month cost (reserved only): $148k. If APAC uses burst at 40% of burst capacity for 14 days, additional burst charges estimate: $18.2k (burst rate 1.2x of base hourly). I've pulled a sample calc into the one-pager for procurement.

Region SOWs: we can do separate SOWs per region to satisfy compliance segmentation. That will add two region-specific exhibits but keep a single master customer agreement if you prefer simpler contract governance.

Next steps: I propose a 30-minute call Friday to agree on final GPU counts and the SOW structure; I can have Markus join to cover runbook and failover timings. Which timezone works best for you?

Regards,
Monica

Attachments: RWI_billing_explainer_for_acme.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Proposal: Reserved GPU Commitment + EU/APAC failover addendum — internal summary / approval request

Looping you both in on Alex's clarifications. ACME is leaning toward: separate region SOWs, wants standby billing clarity, and expects a conservative credit ladder. Two asks for us before we finalize amendment: 

- Legal: can we accept credits capped at 50% as stated and keep the "post-incident validation" clause?
- Ops (Markus): confirm RTO/RPO expectations (90s RTO for session fallback, region routing in 3 tiers) are operationally feasible with current orchestration and whether the warm-standby sizing approach needs automation work (self-heal hooks) before go-live. If ops needs an engineering runbook/timebox, call that out — we should not overpromise.

Please mark approval or list changes and I'll consolidate into a second redline to send to Acme.

Karthik
Head of Sales, North America
Redwood Inference
